clue.text: Ban for Hungary initially took effect after international

indicators.note: after places the effect word behind the international letter in the answer

parts.note: pro means in favour of, so 'for'

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word Hungary

parts.note: brakes or a tax that bit took effect, gripped

explanation.surface: A news item: a ban in Hungary kicked in once an international agreement was reached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is PRO (in favour of), not a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To prohibit is to forbid formally, a verb synonym of the verb ban.

clue.text: Sharp reminder

definitions.meaning: punctual, as in starting at eight o'clock exactly
a cue given to an actor who forgets a line

explanation.surface: A curt nudge.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for punctual and a noun for a cue to jog memory.

clue.text: Honest one struggling to win

indicators.note: struggling suggests something writhing about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A decent person fighting hard for victory.
explanation.definitionFit: In horse racing, a bet placed this way pays only if the horse wins outright.

clue.text: List including band

parts.note: inc. is a short form of including
a band is a stripe or line

explanation.surface: A list of names that includes a musical group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'List' is a verb, to lean, as a ship does.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that lists leans to one side, a verb synonym of slope or tilt.

clue.text: Fashionable to rent in bay

parts.note: in means fashionable
to let means to rent out

explanation.surface: A trendy holiday home available to rent on a bay.
explanation.definitionFit: A small arm of the sea reaching into the coast, a kind of bay.

clue.text: Sharp, a group of detectives in charge

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: A description of a squad of detectives running a case: sharp ones in command.
explanation.definitionFit: An acidic taste or remark is tart and biting, so sharp.

clue.text: Cold drink with favourite item of food

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
rum is a spirit, a drink
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A chilled drink and a favourite snack go together.
explanation.walkthrough: A crumpet is a soft, holey British griddle cake eaten toasted with butter.
explanation.definitionFit: A toasted griddle cake is an example of something you eat.

clue.text: Current doctor, awfully fit

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters are badly placed and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Today's GP is in terrible shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A drift is a slow flow of water or air, a current.

clue.text: Pick up Conservative leaflet

parts.note: a tract is a short pamphlet or leaflet

explanation.surface: Someone collects a Tory party flyer.
explanation.definitionFit: To contract a disease is to catch it, a verb sense of pick up.

clue.text: Biographer of Greek god, endlessly cunning

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the god is cut off

parts.note: Pluto, the ruler of the underworld, also called Pluton by the Greeks
arch means sly, cunning

explanation.surface: A writer of lives of a crafty Greek deity.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek writer of the Parallel Lives was a famous ancient biographer.

clue.text: This is not what it appears to be

definitions.text: This is not what it appears to be

parts.words: This is not what it appears to be
parts.note: the whole clue describes a visual trick in which the eye is deceived by the image

explanation.surface: A warning that something is deceptive.
explanation.definitionFit: A trick of sight shows something differing from reality, so it is literally not what it appears to be.

clue.text: Forecast from pair before proclamation

indicators.note: before puts the pair letters ahead of the proclamation word

parts.note: an edict is an official decree or proclamation

explanation.surface: Two people forecast a result ahead of an official announcement.
explanation.definitionFit: To predict is to foretell, a verb synonym of the verb forecast.

clue.text: One who should be able to give better advice?

definitions.text: One who should be able to give better advice?

parts.words: One who should be able to give better advice?
parts.note: a better here is someone who bets; the racing pundit advises punters on what to back

explanation.surface: Seems to describe someone whose advice ought to improve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' reads as 'superior' but means 'one who bets'.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing pundit supplies betting advice to punters, the people who bet.

clue.text: Arm in arm continuously

definitions.meaning: two people walking linked are side by side, in company
for three days on end, without a break, in unbroken sequence

explanation.surface: A couple strolling arm in arm without a break.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both 'in company with each other' and 'in unbroken succession', as in hours on end.

clue.text: Self-government in order

parts.note: at home means in, as in 'is anyone in?'
a rule is an order or command

explanation.surface: Governing oneself keeps things in order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is not a link word: it means at home.
explanation.definitionFit: The term for a region's governing of its own internal affairs, historically Ireland.

clue.text: Subject to endless choice

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the choice word is cut off

parts.note: your pick is your choice

explanation.surface: Someone is constantly bombarded by an endless set of options.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subject to' looks like one phrase; 'Subject' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is a theme under discussion, a noun synonym of the noun subject.

clue.text: Very poor writer on African river steamship

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
the Nile is the great African river

explanation.surface: An impoverished author aboard a Nile steamer.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no money at all means destitute, extremely poor.

clue.text: Strange order to a fighter in ring

indicators.note: strange means odd, so the letters take an unusual arrangement

explanation.surface: An odd command given to a boxer.
explanation.walkthrough: The ring is a bullring, not a boxing ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullfighter fights in the bullring, so this is one kind of fighter in a ring.

clue.text: Evident through time

parts.note: when something is through it is finished or over

explanation.surface: Something becomes clear over the course of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means openly shown, plain to see, a synonym of evident.

clue.text: Explosive device enlisted men put in depot, nervously

indicators.note: put in places the soldiers' letters inside the rearranged depot
nervously suggests jittery movement, so the letters of depot are shaken up

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Jittery soldiers store a bomb in a depot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enlisted men' are other ranks, the non-officers; 'nervously' scrambles the depot's letters into TPEDO.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-propelled underwater missile is an explosive device.

clue.text: A wild boar found in many a wood

indicators.note: found in places the boar piece inside the many word

parts.note: taken as written
a boar is a kind of hog

explanation.surface: A wild boar is often spotted in the forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wood' is the timber, not a forest; 'many a' tempts as a phrase but the 'a' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahogany is a reddish-brown hardwood timber, an example of wood.

clue.text: Good author of thrillers, I'll wager

definitions.note: the definition is what such a person might say, a noun for one who bets

parts.note: Eric Ambler was a British thriller writer

explanation.surface: Someone betting that a thriller writer is good.
explanation.walkthrough: Eric Ambler wrote spy thrillers such as The Mask of Dimitrios. The definition is the gambler's own words.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who bets would say they will wager, so the phrase stands for a better.

clue.text: Dope test for the nobs?

parts.note: dope and gen both mean information
a try is a test or attempt

explanation.surface: A drug test for the upper classes?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' means inside information, not a drug.
explanation.definitionFit: The landed gentry are the upper classes, slangily called the nobs.

clue.text: Sovereign's agent in capital sent back

indicators.note: sent back means the whole assembly is read backwards
in places the agent word inside the capital word

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital
a rep is a sales representative, an agent

explanation.surface: A monarch's envoy posted in a capital is recalled home.
explanation.walkthrough: ''s' stands for 'is'. REP in ROME gives ROREPME, which 'sent back' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor rules an empire, so he is a sovereign ruler.

clue.text: Haughty, staff round university after power

indicators.note: after places the staff assembly behind the power letter

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for power

indicators.note: round puts the staff letters around the university letter

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: An arrogant academic employee working for a powerful institution.
explanation.definitionFit: Proud and haughty are synonyms, meaning arrogant.

clue.text: Anger shown by siren, one preying ruthlessly on others

parts.note: a vamp is a seductive woman, a siren
ire is anger

explanation.surface: A femme fatale shows her fury while exploiting those around her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown by' is a link word joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloodsucker who exploits others, figuratively a predatory person, as well as the blood-drinking undead.

clue.text: Intense and very very angry, blowing top

indicators.note: blowing top means the first letter is lost

parts.note: livid means furious, very angry

explanation.surface: Someone extremely furious, losing their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing top' (losing one's temper) removes the first letter of LIVID.
explanation.definitionFit: Vivid colours or feelings are strong and bright, so intense.

clue.text: Make every possible effort in Lorna's flat first?

parts.note: Lorna Doone is the heroine of R. D. Blackmore's novel, so Lorna's gives her surname with the possessive S
level means flat, even
best means first, top

explanation.surface: Asks whether a character named Lorna gave her flat the top place.
explanation.walkthrough: Lorna Doone is the title heroine of a classic English romance set on Exmoor.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning to try as hard as one can, to give one's utmost.

clue.text: Tabloid's florid chief

parts.note: a florid complexion is ruddy, red
top means chief, leading

explanation.surface: A tabloid newspaper's boss has a ruddy face.
explanation.walkthrough: ''s' stands for 'is'. British tabloids such as The Sun have red mastheads.
explanation.definitionFit: A British name for a downmarket popular newspaper, after its red masthead.

clue.text: Quite possibly raised abroad, a leader of yours

indicators.note: abroad means all over the place, so the letters of raised are scattered
leader of points to the opening letter of the word yours

explanation.surface: A letter sign-off from someone raised overseas, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A conversational phrase conceding something is probably true, much like perhaps.
